answer: Each agent must lock a scarce, nontransferable bond before it can act. Random audits compare accounts’ actions and evidence; when independent reviewers confirm coordinated duplicate identities, the linked bonds are slashed. This does not prove who a person is, but makes each extra persona require more capital at risk. An attacker must fund many bonds and keep them locked, then may lose them all if coordination is exposed. A relic of past audit records can guide checks as the tide of new accounts rises; jade status grants no exemption.
